assessmentSummary.identity: One exact Source 44 wall-supported bilateral flat-floor standing calf raise begins facing a stable wall with both hands in light continuous contact, both full feet planted about hip-width, and both knees mostly straight without forced locking. Press through both forefeet to raise both heels simultaneously through comfortable plantarflexion, reach a brief untimed top checkpoint, then lower both heels under control to the same full-foot floor contact. One complete rise-and-return cycle is one repetition. Stance width, small foot-angle changes, comfortable range, tempo, the brief non-dose checkpoint, breathing, repetitions, sets, rest, effort, footwear, and delivery context are annotations. Step range, unilateral or alternating action, unsupported balance, bent-knee delivery, external load, a sustained isometric hold, assisted-rise eccentric-only lowering, fast elastic action, locomotion, compound actions, clinical testing, or sport actions change the variant or definition.
currentCardFindings: Source 44 and the older Standing Calf Raise survivor describe the same standing plantarflexion family, while the current rows conflict on slug, support, laterality, start, return, count, and publication semantics. Sources 762, 841, and 1104 are contraction-mode variants, not independent movement definitions.

Earlier automated consolidation correctly preserved several aliases but over-broadened the selectable baseline to unilateral, loaded, isometric, and eccentric names without exact variant contracts. The new survivor keeps those names traceable while selecting only Source 44's supported bilateral flat-floor full cycle.

The inherited participant skill labels, age metadata, publication state, generic performance claims, and old difficulty values are not card-specific approvals. Difficulty is reassessed as exercise complexity and physical difficulty only; participant readiness remains a workout input.

currentCardSnapshot.description: Stand facing a stable wall with both hands in light continuous contact, feet about hip-width on a dry level nonslip floor, the full feet planted, and both knees mostly straight without forced locking. Keeping the wall contact, knee position, foot angle, and body line controlled, press through both forefeet to lift both heels together through comfortable ankle plantarflexion. Reach a brief untimed top checkpoint, then lower both heels under control to the same full-foot floor contact. One complete bilateral lift-and-controlled-return cycle is one repetition. Stance width, small foot-angle changes, comfortable range, tempo, a brief untimed top checkpoint, breathing, repetitions, sets, rest, effort, footwear, and delivery context are annotations. Step range, unilateral or alternating action, unsupported balance, bent-knee delivery, external load, sustained isometric hold, assisted-return eccentric-only work, elastic bouncing, locomotion, compound actions, clinical testing, or sport actions require a separately reviewed variant or definition.

alternateAssessments.name: Wall-Supported Bilateral Standing Calf Raise
alternateAssessments.rationale: This descriptive name makes support and laterality explicit without changing the task.

alternateAssessments.name: Comfortable Stance Width
alternateAssessments.rationale: Small stance-width adjustments preserve support, action, and count.

alternateAssessments.name: Small Foot-Angle Adjustment
alternateAssessments.rationale: Record a comfortable foot angle without turning it into a targeted or different exercise.

alternateAssessments.name: Comfortable Heel-Raise Height
alternateAssessments.rationale: A smaller active range changes amplitude without changing the cycle.

alternateAssessments.name: Controlled Rise and Return Tempo
alternateAssessments.rationale: Tempo changes exposure while preserving the complete cycle.

alternateAssessments.name: Brief Untimed Top Checkpoint
alternateAssessments.rationale: A brief checkpoint is not an isometric task unless prescribed by time or effort.

alternateAssessments.name: Breathing Prompt
alternateAssessments.rationale: Breathing changes delivery rather than identity.

alternateAssessments.name: Repetitions Sets Rest or Effort Target
alternateAssessments.rationale: Volume, recovery, and effort change dosage rather than identity.

alternateAssessments.name: Footwear or Approved Barefoot Context
alternateAssessments.rationale: Footwear is an annotation only when traction, heel geometry, forefoot flexibility, range, and mechanics remain valid.

alternateAssessments.name: Preparation Capacity or General Context
alternateAssessments.rationale: Workout context is a delivery profile unless a physical action is added.

alternateAssessments.name: Step Calf Raise Through Below-Neutral Range
alternateAssessments.rationale: A step adds below-neutral range, edge geometry, equipment, and fall consequences.

alternateAssessments.name: Single-Leg Standing Calf Raise
alternateAssessments.rationale: Unilateral loading changes force, balance, asymmetry, fatigue, failure, and count.

alternateAssessments.name: Alternating Standing Calf Raise
alternateAssessments.rationale: Alternation changes timing, unilateral exposure, side order, and count.

alternateAssessments.name: Unsupported Standing Calf Raise
alternateAssessments.rationale: Removing wall support changes balance, failure consequence, and supervision.

alternateAssessments.name: Externally Loaded Standing Calf Raise
alternateAssessments.rationale: External resistance changes implement handling, load path, setup, fatigue, and failure response.

alternateAssessments.name: Standing Calf Raise Sustained Top Hold
alternateAssessments.rationale: A prescribed hold changes contraction mode, endpoint, dose unit, fatigue, and count.

alternateAssessments.name: Assisted-Rise Eccentric-Only Standing Calf Lower
alternateAssessments.rationale: Assistance into the top and a prescribed negative change return strategy, tempo, load, and count.

alternateAssessments.name: Fast Elastic Calf Raise or Rebound
alternateAssessments.rationale: Fast elastic intent changes stretch-shortening demand, contact behavior, impact, and stop rules.

alternateAssessments.name: Bent-Knee Soleus Raise
alternateAssessments.rationale: A materially bent knee changes support, muscle-length context, loading, and task contract.

alternateAssessments.name: Seated Soleus or Dumbbell Calf Raise
alternateAssessments.rationale: Seated knee-flexed support and thigh loading change the base, force path, balance, and logistics.

alternateAssessments.name: Wall-Supported Tibialis Raise
alternateAssessments.rationale: The heels stay planted while the forefeet lift through dorsiflexion.

alternateAssessments.name: Knee-to-Wall Ankle Rocker
alternateAssessments.rationale: The heel remains planted while the knee travels forward and returns through dorsiflexion.

alternateAssessments.name: Wall Calf Stretch Hold
alternateAssessments.rationale: A split-stance static lengthened-position hold uses time rather than bilateral repetitions.

alternateAssessments.name: Ankle Pogo in Place
alternateAssessments.rationale: Pogos add elastic impact, rebound, possible flight, landing, and contact counting.

alternateAssessments.name: Walking Knee Hug to Calf Raise
alternateAssessments.rationale: Walking, unilateral balance, knee-hug action, and calf raise form a compound locomotor sequence.

alternateAssessments.name: Short Foot to Calf Raise
alternateAssessments.rationale: A separately cued foot-intrinsic action precedes the calf raise, creating a compound sequence.
